g.text: One operation of each kind in the view-gate model
A checkpoint takes its gate first and the owner mutex second, the owner checks before it captures,
and an acknowledged caller keeps its gate until it has installed the answer;
a reset and a spawn change only the views; close and reopen need a quiescent owner
CallCheckpoint(view, permit): the idle caller takes the
free gate of its permit, its own view's gate in a correct
call, before it calls the owner.
TakeMutex(view): the view now holds the owner mutex.
Holding it, the owner never waits for a gate (LockOrder).

ReturnCall(view): the mutex is freed. A call that is not acknowledged
becomes idle and frees every gate that it holds; an acknowledged call
keeps its gate and enters the stage install. A gate marked pending
From the result "acknowledged" until InstallView the
caller holds its own gate, so no operation of the view
runs on the store that the answer supersedes.
"release-before-install" free the gate early and violate it
the witness NeverInstalledAnswer reaches the stage install.

ResetView(view, target), when the view's caller is idle
and its own gate is free: the view's base becomes the
target, and nothing else changes. The owner's root stays
A spawn reads nothing of the owner: a view
spawned from a stale attachment carries
the stale incarnation, and a checkpoint
through its own gate is refused with
CallSpawn(view), when both callers are idle and both
gates are free: the other view's attachment becomes a
copy of this view's incarnation, base and session
CloseOwner, only on a live, quiescent owner below its session bound:
live becomes false and the incarnation advances by one, so every
attachment taken before the close fails the incarnation check.
A view that kept its old attachment is
ReopenOwner(view, incarnation), only on a closed, quiescent owner:
live becomes true, the incarnation advances by one again
(FreshIncarnation), the session advances, and the view attaches
at the owner's root with the new incarnation and session.
